# isAbsolute

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is an absolute path.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isAbsolute() — Checks whether a value is an absolute path. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isAbsolute(path: string): path is string;
```

A path that starts at a root: a leading `/`, or a scheme such as `https://` or `mailto:`. Everything else, the empty string included, is relative.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description        |
| :-------- | :------- | :----------------- |
| `path`    | `string` | The path to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is an absolute path; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `path` to `string` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isAbsolute("/var/log"); // => true
isAbsolute("https://example.com/a"); // => true
isAbsolute("mailto:a@example.com"); // => true
isAbsolute("docs/readme.md"); // => false
isAbsolute("./a"); // => false
isAbsolute(""); // => false
```
